title: Project-Based Learning & Industry Connections in Nanofabrication
description: Module 5 focuses on project-based learning (PBL) in nanofabrication and fostering industry connections through practical, real-world projects and educational resources.

sections.title: Project-Based Learning in Nanofabrication
sections.content: Project-based learning (PBL) immerses students in hands-on, interdisciplinary projects that bridge theoretical knowledge with practical applications. PBL fosters problem-solving, creativity, and collaboration—essential skills for advancing nanotechnology innovation and addressing complex challenges in industry and society.

sections.title: Example Projects
sections.content:
- Nanorobots for Sustainability: Design and prototype autonomous nanoscale robots for environmental monitoring, pollutant degradation, or precision agriculture.
- Nano-Medical Devices: Develop models or simulations for nanoscale targeted drug delivery systems, nanosensors for diagnostics, or nano-enabled tissue engineering scaffolds.
- Smart Textiles: Investigate integration of nanoscale sensors, coatings, or conductive fibers to create textiles with responsive features like temperature regulation, health monitoring, or adaptive camouflage.

sections.title: Competition and Showcase
sections.content:
Students are encouraged to communicate their work via video presentations, posters, or virtual showcases. These venues help:
- Encourage professional scientific communication skills.
- Facilitate peer and faculty feedback.
- Connect researchers, industry mentors, and funding opportunities.
- Simulate real-world scientific conferences or startup pitch events.
